correctness.rationale: The scalar unit is a central direct factor and the other factor is the affine group. For a fixed affine element (t,u), commutation is (t−1)z=us with 1+s a unit. The unrestricted kernel has size q^(m+min(ν(t−1),ν(u))). When ν(u)<ν(t−1), a forbidden s of residue −1 is impossible; otherwise each forbidden s has q^ν(t−1) lifts in z. The centralizers and both class families follow. Under conjugation the multiplier is fixed and the translation becomes yu+(1−t)z with y a unit, so the valuation bins used to divide by class size are invariant. A character nontrivial on the socle yields an injective additive-dual parameterization, since each nonzero ideal contains the socle; induction from unit stabilizers gives one layer of q^j irreducibles per valuation with orbit degree w_j, besides the zero-orbit U linear characters of the affine factor. The scalar factor replicates each degree U times. The q=2 overlap of degree one and the extra socle-sized affine center are correctly included. The class total, order, commuting probability and complex algebra decomposition then follow. An independent orbit enumeration on Z/4 and F4[e]/e² reproduced both spectra; the latter includes nonprime residue size. In particular it gave class counts {1:12,3:12,4:36,12:48,16:96} and degrees {1:144,3:48,12:12} for q=4, m=2.
residual_risks: Finite orbit cases do not prove the all-ring claim; the invariant-bin and little-group arguments do. The sentence describing the affine linear characters in the proof is read by orbit layer, as the Finding explicitly requires.

evidence: The affine record gives one size-q^(m−k) class per multiplier of k=ν(1−t), and one class of size w_h for each h<k, for arbitrary length; it also classifies affine character degrees.

evidence: Summing the affine large-class branch over multipliers of valuation j gives v_j; summing its size-w_h branch over k>h gives q^(m−h−1); the scalar factor supplies U copies of each. The affine degree layers U and q^j multiply to U² and Uq^j. Center, class number, commuting probability and complex algebra then follow directly.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Both centerpiece distributions and the corollaries follow without any new mathematical lemma. Additive-character orbits also have substantial antecedents, but that alone would not settle the internal class-size question.
